body: An expensed cost reduces CFO; a capitalised one goes to CFI (capex, intangible additions) so CFO and EBITDA both look better. Levers: development/software capitalisation (Ind AS 38), borrowing costs (Ind AS 23), pre-operative expenses parked in CWIP, contract-acquisition costs (Ind AS 115/ASC 340-40), and outright line-cost capitalisation (WorldCom ~$3.8bn in 2001-02 per SEC complaint). Tests: (1) judge cash generation on FCF after capitalised intangibles; (2) capex and intangible additions vs depreciation, vs peers, and vs own history - capex rising without revenue growth is a flag; (3) capitalised borrowing cost / total finance cost >20% (Ind AS 23 note); (4) intangible additions vs cash R&D in MD&A/con-call. Indian specific: Schedule III (from FY22) requires ageing of CWIP and intangible assets under development.
title: Capitalising costs moves expenses out of CFO and the P&L - use FCF, not CFO

body: Cohen and Frazzini, 'Economic Links and Predictable Returns' (Journal of Finance 63(4), 2008; ~1,360 citations), US 1980-2004, using mandatory disclosures of major customers (more than 10% of sales). When a major customer's stock moves, the supplier's stock follows over the next month: a long-short portfolio buying suppliers whose customers had the best returns the prior month and shorting those whose customers had the worst earned about 1.5% a month (~18% a year), unexplained by standard factors. The lag is larger when fewer mutual funds hold both firms, which is consistent with investors' limited attention. Replicated: yes; Menzly-Ozbas (2010) find industry-level supply-chain momentum, and later papers find it across countries, though it has weakened in US large caps. Use for us: this is a scuttlebutt-friendly structural edge. Indian annual reports and DRHPs often name major customers (auto ancillaries -> Maruti/M&M/Tata Motors, EMS -> Dixon clients, capital goods -> PSU utilities, CDMOs -> innovator pharma). Map supplier-customer links for watchlist names. When a big customer reports strong volumes, guidance or capex, or a US customer reports, check whether the Indian small-cap supplier has repriced. Monthly Vahan, SIAM and customer releases are leading data for suppliers; link insight:vahan-vs-siam-channel-check.
title: Economic links (Cohen-Frazzini 2008): customer news reaches supplier prices with a lag; ~1.5%/month long-short
